sentences.text: 1 2. Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel for the applicant-accused.
3. Mr. Akshay Latwal, learned Assistant Government Advocate for the respondent no.1.
4. Mr. Shashank Pandey, learned counsel for the respondent no.2-victim.
5. Mr. Akshay Pradhan, Advocate submitted that according to the alleged victim (PW1), the respondent no.2, her date of birth is 11.05.2007 (Leaving Certificate- Annexure No.3).
She has stated in her examination that the applicant did not forcefully take her to Baghpat.
He had not established any physical relationship with her.
She has married the applicant after attaining majority.
She got married to the applicant on 08.06.2025, and, now they are living happily as wife and husband.
6. The applicant - accused and the respondent no.2-victim are present together through video conferencing.
The applicant is identified by Mr. Akshay Pradhan, Advocate.
The respondent no.2-victim is identified by Mr. Shashank Pandey, Advocate.
7. Both, the applicant and the respondent no.2 submitted that they have married and they are living happily as husband and wife.
The respondent no.2 has 2025:UHC:8803 requested to quash the entire proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.33 of 2024.
8. Mr. Akshay Latwal, Assistant Government Advocate has opposed the said request of the respondent no.2 on the ground that the offences are non-compoundable.

9. Though this Court would normally be hesitant to quash the proceedings under Sections 363, 366,
376 of the IPC and the proceedings under the provisions of the Act, 2012, but, it is noticed that the applicant and the victim are living happily as husband and wife.
In these circumstances, in case, the proceedings are allowed to continue, it would amount to denial of complete justice to the parties.
Therefore, it is a case, in which the inherent jurisdiction of this Court should be exercised to do real and substantial justice.

10. Considering the totality of the matter, this Court is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the entire proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.33 of 2024, "State vs. Pardeshi", pending before the court of Additional District and Sessions Judge/Fast Track Special Court, Roorkee,
District Haridwar, are quashed.
